title: Add a Delegate to the Template
scenario: It is 6:35 AM. Last month a brief sat unapproved for forty minutes because the Desk Manager was unreachable and nobody knew who else could sign. The desk agreed the approval template itself must name a delegate. Evolve the governed format: add the field, bump the version, note the change.
input:
Amendment to the Brief Approval Request template (currently v1.0.0):
Every approval template must name a DELEGATE - the role that decides when the primary approver is unavailable. For brief approvals the delegate is the Deputy Desk Manager. The response deadline stays 30 minutes. Owner remains the Risk Desk Lead; changes still require Desk Manager sign-off. Record as version 1.1.0 with a change note explaining why the field was added.
instructions: Carry forward the unchanged fields from v1.0.0 (name, owner, approver, subject format, deadline).
Add the delegate field the amendment requires.
Bump the version and write the changeNote.
Validate when every field is filled.
copilotPrompt: Amend a governed approval template: keep templateName, owner, approver, subjectFormat, and responseDeadlineMinutes from v1.0.0; add a delegate field (Deputy Desk Manager); bump version to 1.1.0; and write a changeNote explaining the delegate was added after an approver was unreachable.
successMessage: Template amended. When an approver goes quiet, the workflow now knows - from the template itself - who decides instead.

intro.heading: Before you build: formats evolve like policies

sections.title: The gap this field closes
sections.body: An unreachable approver is not an edge case - it is a certainty over enough mornings. Naming the delegate IN the template means the exception path is decided before the exception, by governance rather than by whoever is panicking at 6:40.

sections.title: Amendments carry their history
sections.body: Same discipline as the threshold policy change: unchanged fields carry forward, the new field is added, the version bumps to 1.1.0, and the changeNote records why. A format whose changes are explained can be trusted through its whole history.

sections.title: Watch this field get used
sections.body: On this tier's approval lesson, the Desk Manager is out of office - and the out-of-office reply points at exactly the delegate you are naming now. Governance fields earn their keep on the bad mornings.

takeaway.heading: Template amended
points: You evolved a governed format the same way policies evolve: carry forward, add, bump, explain.
The delegate is now a FIELD, so the exception path is machine-readable instead of tribal knowledge.
The changeNote preserves the incident that motivated the change - future maintainers inherit the reasoning.
This tier's approval handoff uses this exact field when the Desk Manager's out-of-office hits.
The workflow can now survive an unavailable approver by design, not by improvisation.
